title: Typing context with no good default

slides.say: If your context has a sensible default, TypeScript infers its type. The tricky case is when there's no default.
With a real default, like light, the type comes straight from create context.
No sensible default? Use null, and say so in the type: user, or null.
Then wrap it in a custom Hook that checks for null and throws. After the check, the Hook returns a plain user, so no consumer has to deal with null.
